  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Image resize service", "URL fetcher", "Resizer", "Internal metadata service"],
    "dataStores": ["Internal databases"],
    "externalServices": ["Arbitrary attacker-supplied URLs"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Caller to image service", "Image service to VPC internal services", "Image service to public internet"],
    "dataClasses": ["secrets"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Server-side request forgery reaches internal services inside the VPC",
      "scenario": "A caller passes a URL pointing at the internal metadata service or a database admin endpoint (for example http://169.254.169.254/ or http://metadata.internal/). The service downloads it from inside the VPC, where those hosts have no external exposure, and returns the response body as an 'image'. The attacker reads cloud instance credentials or internal metadata they could never reach directly.",
      "component": "URL fetcher",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL, resizes it and returns it" },
        { "quote": "It runs inside our VPC next to the internal metadata service and databases." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.5.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-918"],
      "plainLanguage": "The service will fetch any address you give it, including private internal ones, and hand you back what it found.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Validate fetch targets against an allowlist and block internal address ranges",
        "given": "the image resize service runs inside the VPC alongside internal services",
        "when": "a caller supplies a URL whose resolved IP is private, loopback, link-local or cloud metadata",
        "then": "the fetch is refused before any connection is made and the request is rejected with a generic error"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Non-image responses and error details leak internal content back to the caller",
      "scenario": "Even where resizing fails, the attacker learns about internal systems: distinct error messages and timings reveal which internal hosts and ports exist, and any response that happens to parse as an image (or is echoed in an error) returns internal data verbatim. This turns the resize endpoint into an internal port and host scanner.",
      "component": "Image resize service response path",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "downloads the image from that URL, resizes it and returns it" },
        { "quote": "next to the internal metadata service and databases" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.5.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-209"],
      "plainLanguage": "Error messages and timing differences tell an attacker which internal machines and ports are alive.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Return uniform errors and only valid re-encoded images",
        "given": "a fetch to a supplied URL fails or returns content that is not a valid image",
        "when": "the service responds to the caller",
        "then": "it returns a single generic error with no upstream status, body or host detail, and never echoes fetched bytes"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Redirect and DNS rebinding bypass any URL check done before the fetch",
      "scenario": "The attacker supplies a public URL that passes validation, then the HTTP client follows a 302 to http://metadata.internal, or the hostname resolves to a public IP at check time and a private IP at connect time. The design validates nothing and the fetcher is described as simply downloading from the URL, so the internal target is reached despite any naive allowlist.",
      "component": "URL fetcher HTTP client",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "medium", "reach": "all", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The image service accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.5.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-350"],
      "plainLanguage": "A safe-looking link can bounce the service to an internal address after the check has passed.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Pin the connection to the validated address and control redirects",
        "given": "a supplied URL has passed allowlist and private-range validation",
        "when": "the service opens the connection or receives a redirect response",
        "then": "it connects to the exact validated IP, disables automatic redirects, and re-validates any redirect target before following it"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Internal non-HTTP services written to via forged requests",
      "scenario": "The attacker points the URL at an internal database, cache or queue port inside the VPC. Because the service connects from a trusted network position and the design states databases sit next to it, a crafted URL (unexpected scheme, embedded newlines or credentials) can deliver attacker-controlled bytes to an unauthenticated internal listener, changing stored data rather than only reading it.",
      "component": "URL fetcher to internal databases",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "medium", "reach": "all", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "It runs inside our VPC next to the internal metadata service and databases." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.5.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-918"],
      "plainLanguage": "The fetcher can be aimed at internal databases and used to send them attacker-chosen data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict schemes and egress from the resize service",
        "given": "the resize service needs to fetch images from approved sources only",
        "when": "a URL uses a scheme other than https, or targets a port outside the approved set",
        "then": "the request is rejected, and network egress rules deny the service any connection to internal service ports"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Decompression bomb and oversized downloads exhaust memory and CPU",
      "scenario": "A caller supplies a URL serving a small file that decodes to an enormous bitmap, or an endless stream. The service downloads and resizes it with no stated size, pixel or timeout limit, so a handful of requests consume all memory and CPU and take the resize service down for every internal consumer.",
      "component": "Resizer",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "availability" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "downloads the image from that URL, resizes it and returns it" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-409"],
      "plainLanguage": "A tiny file that expands into a giant image can crash the service for everyone.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce download, dimension and time limits on every resize",
        "given": "the service is fetching and decoding a remote image",
        "when": "the download exceeds the byte limit, the decoded pixel count exceeds the limit, or the operation exceeds its timeout",
        "then": "the fetch and decode are aborted and buffers are released before the limit is breached"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Unauthenticated internal callers can drive the fetcher",
      "scenario": "The design names no authentication or authorisation for the endpoint; it only accepts a URL parameter. Any workload or person on the internal network, including a compromised low-value service or a developer machine, can call it and use its privileged network position to fetch internal resources on their behalf, with no caller identity recorded to attribute the abuse.",
      "component": "Image resize service endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The image service accepts a URL parameter" },
        { "quote": "It runs inside our VPC" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anything on the internal network can use this service as a tunnel, and nobody can tell who did.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Authenticate and attribute every resize request",
        "given": "the resize service is reachable from inside the VPC",
        "when": "a request arrives without a valid service identity",
        "then": "it is rejected, and accepted requests record the caller identity with the requested URL"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Fetched internal content cached or served to later callers",
      "scenario": "Resized output is returned directly with no stated keying or isolation. If a response produced from an internal URL is cached by the service or a CDN in front of it, another caller requesting the same path receives content derived from internal systems, widening a single forged fetch into exposure to every consumer of the service.",
      "component": "Image resize service response path",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "medium", "reach": "many", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "resizes it and returns it" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V3.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-524"],
      "plainLanguage": "Internal data pulled in once could be stored and handed to other users later.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Do not cache responses derived from unvalidated fetches",
        "given": "a resize response has been generated from a caller-supplied URL",
        "when": "the response is returned",
        "then": "it is marked non-cacheable unless the source URL is on the approved allowlist, and cache keys include the full source URL and caller scope"
      }
    }
  ]
